subject: Revenue & Packaging Annex — minimums, anchoring mechanics, and liability carveouts
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@mapscape.com>, Dana Li <dana.li@mapscape.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Revenue & Packaging Annex — minimums, anchoring mechanics, and liability carveouts

Hi Oliver / Dana —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching the latest pricing schedule and a draft annex with our proposal for how packaging minimums, anchoring, and liability caps interact. Two quick asks so we can align with legal and procurement: 

1) Can you confirm MapsCape's expected monthly SKU mix (attached table in pricing_schedule_v3) so we can validate the proposed "anchored minimums" math?
2) On liability: you flagged concern about a fixed cap that exceeds committed spend during ramp months. Our legal suggested a sliding cap tied to rolling 90-day committed baseline — attaching a redline (redline_annex_v2.docx). Would that be acceptable as a compromise?

Proposed next steps: if you confirm the SKU mix by EOD Wed, I'll have Markus and Laura fold in the conservative language and then share a final redline for signature. If procurement needs a firm # for execution, we can propose a short-term carveout for the first 3 months of the term.

Attachments: pricing_schedule_v3.pdf (pricing table), redline_annex_v2.docx (markup)

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0199

From: Oliver Grant <oliver@mapscape.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Li <dana.li@mapscape.com>, Procurement <procurement@mapscape.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revenue & Packaging Annex — minimums, anchoring mechanics, and liability carveouts

Karthik —

Appreciate the summary and the files. Quick notes after a run-through of the schedule: 

- SKU mix: see attached export from our billing system (note line items 2003/2004 are seasonal and will skew month 2). We can provide a normalized 3‑month baseline but need any "anchored minimum" to allow for that seasonality.
- Liability cap: we cannot accept a cap that is a multiple of committed spend for the first 60 days; procurement will push back. A rolling baseline approach sounds reasonable but needs a clear floor — e.g., at least 60% of committed monthly baseline so we still have predictable exposure.
- Packaging/pack sizes: if you expect customers to convert between SKUs, we need a reconciliation mechanism (true-up within 30 days).

I'll loop in Dana for legal specifics; procurement wants final redline by next Tues to keep our Q4 procurement cycle on track.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform Partnerships, MapsCape
oliver@mapscape.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@mapscape.com>, Dana Li <dana.li@mapscape.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revenue & Packaging Annex — minimums, anchoring mechanics, and liability carveouts

Oliver — thanks for the quick turn. I pulled together a short proposed text for the annex that reflects the rolling baseline + seasonal floor approach we discussed. I'm pasting it below and attaching a plaintext snippet (karthik_proposed_annex_snippet.txt) to make markup easier for your counsel.

---- proposed snippet (plain language) ----
"For the first 90 days of the Term, committed monthly baseline shall be calculated as the average of invoiced SKU units per month as reflected in the Pricing Schedule. For months where invoiced SKU units are more than 25% below the baseline due to seasonality or product migration, the Parties agree to a seasonal floor equal to 60% of the committed monthly baseline for purposes of calculating minimum fees and any associated remedies. The liability cap for direct damages will be the lesser of (i) the aggregate amounts actually paid by Customer under this Agreement in the immediately preceding 90-day period, or (ii) 6 months' committed baseline revenue calculated at the then-applicable pricing schedule."

---- end snippet ----

If that reads OK to MapsCape, Laura/Markus — can you confirm whether the language is legally acceptable or propose alternative metrics (e.g., 120-day lookback, 50% seasonal floor, etc.)? My preference is to keep the math anchored to actual invoiced units rather than an escalator percentage to keep it auditable.

Next step from our side: I can produce a worked example mapping their SKU export to our pricing table so procurement has the visibility for the finance committee. Planning to have a final redline up by Tues if we get confirmation today.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver@mapscape.com>, Dana Li <dana.li@mapscape.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revenue & Packaging Annex — minimums, anchoring mechanics, and liability carveouts

Karthik / all —

Read through the proposed snippet. High-level: this is a pragmatic compromise and should address MapsCape's seasonality concern while preserving Redwood's exposure limits. A few legal refinements I recommend before we issue a formal redline: 

1) Define "invoiced SKU units" precisely — suggest: "units invoiced to Customer under the Pricing Schedule, excluding credits, refunds, and one-off promotional SKUs."
2) Replace 'first 90 days' with 'first billing quarter' to align to standard accounting constructs; otherwise parties will disagree on start/end.
3) For the liability cap, suggest a formula-based cap but with a hard-stop exclusion for willful misconduct and gross negligence: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Party's liability for willful misconduct or gross negligence shall be limited."

Proposed legal redline text (ready to drop into your doc):

"Committed Monthly Baseline" means the trailing 90-day average of units invoiced to Customer under the Pricing Schedule, excluding credits, refunds, and promotional SKUs. For billing periods where invoiced units are less than 75% of the Committed Monthly Baseline due to bona fide seasonality or deliberate SKU migration agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties shall apply a Seasonal Floor equal to 60% of the Committed Monthly Baseline solely for calculation of minimum fees.

"Liability Cap": The aggregate liability of either Party for direct damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the lesser of (i) the total amounts paid by Customer to Redwood under this Agreement in the 90 days preceding the event giving rise to liability, or (ii) an amount equal to six (6) times the Committed Monthly Baseline computed at the then-applicable pricing. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitations set forth in this section shall not apply to liability resulting from a Party's willful misconduct or gross negligence, nor shall they apply to claims for personal injury or breaches of confidentiality obligations.

If that language is acceptable I will inline-markup redline_annex_v2.docx and send for signature via DocuSign link (attached). If MapsCape needs a different lookback or floor percentage, tell us which metric procurement has mandate for and we'll adapt.

I'll wait for confirmation to finalize and route for signature.

-Markus
